current_disclosures.summary: Data Center and AI (DCAI) revenue increased $145 million from 2023, primarily due to a 11% increase in server ASPs driven by a higher mix of high core count products. This ASP growth offset an 8% decrease in server volume caused by lower demand and competitive pressures. Other DCAI product revenue decreased $196 million to $2.7 billion, primarily due to 5G customers tempering purchases to reduce existing inventories.

comparisons.peer_summary: Semiconductor solutions segment net revenue increased due to strong demand for AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for broadband and server storage. Infrastructure software segment net revenue increased primarily due to contributions from VMware.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom provide specific drivers for their Data Center/Semiconductor Solutions revenue trends in 2024, highlighting a divergence in server market dynamics. Intel reports a decrease in server volume (-37%) due to softening CPU demand, while Broadcom reports growth in AI networking products that was only partially offset by lower server storage demand. This suggests a bifurcation in the data center market where traditional CPU/server storage demand weakened (Intel) while AI-specific networking demand strengthened (Broadcom).

sentences.text: ▪DCAI revenue decreased $4.2 billion from 2022, driven by a decrease in server revenue. Server volume decreased 37% from 2022, due to lower demand in a softening CPU data center market. Server ASPs increased 20% from 2022, primarily due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer-related revenue and a higher mix of high core count products.

Net revenue from our semiconductor solutions segment increased due to strong product demand for our networking products, primarily AI networking products, partially offset by lower demand for our broadband and server storage products.
